title: bls12-381-g1-ecdlp-plain: deterministic truncated BSGS with a hashed baby table

claims.statement: For uniform x in [0,r), given T=[x]P0 in BLS12-381 G1 with no auxiliary powers and no n parameter, the deterministic truncated baby-step/giant-step algorithm fully specified in proof.md returns x with probability at least 0.41 (exactly (m*h+m-1)/r over the uniform challenge, with m=h=0x6e4ed412a3c552fd2d010d8328cef768) using at most 2^127.875678 total BLS12-381 G1 target-group-operation equivalents, including preprocessing, baby-table construction, hashed lookup, verification and output. Peak memory is at most 2^133.152873 bytes; preprocessing is at most 2^126.876464 target-group-operation equivalents and is included in total work; nonuniform advice is at most 2^0 bytes and is included in memory. This is a classical cold attack with no uncharged advice, no quantum steps and no heuristic assumptions; the exponential memory is required by the construction. This is an analytic generic accounting claim, not a claim of novelty or of practical execution.
